result.topic_en: Faint pencil calculations evaluating integrals of the form $\int_{-\pi-x}^{\pi-x} e^{(k-n)yi}/(1-e^{-yi})\,dy$ via the substitution $z=e^{yi}$, expanding the results in series with $\Pi$ (Gauss's factorial function) and $(1+e^{xi})$, followed by manipulations of factorial-type sums involving $nn\alpha-m+\nu$.

methods.what: Summing a geometric series in the integrand to convert a sum of Fourier-type integrals into a single integral with kernel $1/(1-e^{-yi})$
methods.quote: $\sum_{n,0}^{\infty} e^{kxi}\int_{-\pi-x}^{\pi-x} e^{kyi} e^{-nyi}\,\partial y = e^{kxi}\int_{-\pi-x}^{\pi-x} e^{(k-n)yi}\frac{1}{1-e^{-yi}}\,\partial y$

methods.what: Substitution $z=e^{yi}$ turning the integral into $\int z^{n-k-1}/(1-z)\,dz$
Expansion of the incomplete integral $\int_0^{e^{xi}} z^{n-k-1}/(1+z)\,dz$ as a series in powers of $1/(1+e^{xi})$ with factorial (Pi-function) coefficients, via repeated integration by parts
Resulting series representation involving $2\sin\pi k$ and powers of $(e^{-xi}+1)$
Functional equation of the Pi (factorial) function
Rewritten sum with partial-fraction factor $1/(n(nn\alpha-m-\nu))$ and local approximation near $nn\alpha=m+\nu$
